questions.solution:
Ancient Indian temples are classified in three broad types. Three main style of temple architecture are the Nagara or the Northern style, the Dravida or the Southern style and the Vesara or Mixed style.
The temples of North and South India were distinguished on the basis of some specific features like sikhara and gateways. questions.q: Which one of the following is not an igneous rock?
questions.solution: Igneous rocks form from when hot, molten rock crystallizes and solidifies. The melt originates deep within the Earth near active plate boundaries or hot spots, then rises toward the surface. Igneous rocks are divided into two groups, intrusive or extrusive, depending upon where the molten rock solidifies. Examples of intrusive igneous rocks are diorite, gabbro, granite, pegmatite, and peridotite. Extrusive igneous rocks erupt onto the surface, where they cool quickly to form small crystals.

questions.q: Which one of the following is correct in respect of the function $f(\mathrm{x})=\mathrm{x}(\mathrm{x}-1)(\mathrm{x}+1)$ ?
options: The local maximum value is larger than local minimum value
The local maximum value is smaller than local minimum value
The function has no local maximum
The function has no local minimum
questions.solution:
$f(x)=x(x-1)(x+1)=x\left(x^2-1\right)$
Differentiating, we get
$f^{\prime}(x)=x(2 x)+\left(x^2-1\right)=2 x^2+x^2-1=3 x^2-1$
Again differentiating
$f^{\prime \prime}(x)=6 x\operatorname{At}^{\prime}(x)=0 \Rightarrow 3 x^2-1=0 \Rightarrow x^2=\frac{1}{3} \Rightarrow x= \pm \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$
Maximum value of $f(x)=f\left(\frac{-1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)=\frac{-1}{\sqrt{3}}\left(\left(\frac{-1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)^2-1\right)=\frac{-1}{\sqrt{3}}\left(\frac{1}{3}-1\right)=\frac{-1}{\sqrt{3}}\left(\frac{-2}{3}\right)=\frac{2}{3 \sqrt{3}}$
Minimum value of $f(x)=f\left(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\left(\frac{1}{3}-1\right)=\frac{-2}{3 \sqrt{3}}$

questions.q: The value of $\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{4}} \sqrt{\tan \mathrm{x}} d x+\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{4}} \sqrt{\cot \mathrm{x}} d x$ is equal to

$\begin{aligned} & \int_0^{\frac{\pi}{4}} \sqrt{\tan x} d x+\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{4}} \sqrt{\cot x} \cdot d x \\ & =\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{4}}(\sqrt{\tan x}+\sqrt{\cot x}) d x\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{4}}\left(\frac{\sqrt{\sin x}}{\sqrt{\cos x}}+\frac{\sqrt{\cos x}}{\sqrt{\sin x}}\right) d x \\ & =\int_0^{\frac{\pi}{4}} \frac{\sin x+\cos x}{\sqrt{\sin x} \cdot \sqrt{\cos x}} \cdot d x\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =\sqrt{2} \int_0^{\frac{\pi}{4}} \frac{(\sin x+\cos x)}{\left(\sqrt{1-\left(\sin ^2 x+\cos ^2 x-2 \sin x \cos x\right)}\right)} \cdot d x \\ & =\sqrt{2} \int_0^{\frac{\pi}{4}} \frac{(\sin x+\cos x)}{\sqrt{1-(\sin x-\cos x)^2}} \cdot d x\end{aligned}$
Put $\sin \mathrm{x}-\cos \mathrm{x}=\mathrm{t} \Rightarrow(\cos \mathrm{x}+\sin \mathrm{x}) d \mathrm{~d}=\mathrm{dt}$ 
When $x=0, t=-1$ and $x=\frac{\pi}{4}, t=0$.
$\begin{aligned} & =\sqrt{2} \int_{-1}^0 \frac{1}{\sqrt{1-\mathrm{t}^2}} \cdot \mathrm{dt}=\sqrt{2}\left(\sin ^{-1} \mathrm{t}\right)_{-1}^0 \\ & =\sqrt{2}\left[\sin ^{-1}(0)-\sin ^{-1}(-1)\right] \\ & =\sqrt{2}\left[0-\left(\frac{-\pi}{2}\right)\right]=\frac{\pi}{\sqrt{2}}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The system of equations $k x+y+z=1, x+k y+z=k$ and $x+y+k z=k^2$ has no solution if $k$ equals
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & k x+y+z=1 \\ & x+k y+z=k \\ & x+y+k z=k^2\end{aligned}$
These equations will have no solution of $\left|\begin{array}{lll}\mathrm{k} & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & \mathrm{k} & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & \mathrm{k}\end{array}\right|=0$.
$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \mathrm{k}\left(\mathrm{k}^2-1\right)-1(\mathrm{k}-1)+(1-\mathrm{k})=0 \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{k}(\mathrm{k}+1)(\mathrm{k}-1)-1(\mathrm{k}-1)-(\mathrm{k}-1)=0 \\ & \Rightarrow(\mathrm{k}-1)[\mathrm{k}(\mathrm{k}+1)-1-1]=0\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}&\Rightarrow(\mathrm{k}-1)\left(\mathrm{k}^2+\mathrm{k}-2\right)=0 \\& \Rightarrow \mathrm{k}=1 \text { or }-2 \end{aligned}$
For $\mathrm{k}=1$, all equations are same and have infinite solution. So, for $\mathrm{k}=-2$, equations have no solution.

$\begin{aligned} & \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{y \phi^{\prime}(x)-y^2}{\phi(x)}=\frac{y \phi^{\prime}(x)}{\phi(x)}-\frac{y^2}{\phi(x)} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{d y}{d x}=\frac{y^2 \cdot \phi^{\prime}(x)}{y \cdot \phi(x)}-\frac{y^2}{\phi(x)}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{y^2}\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)=\frac{\phi^{\prime}(x)}{y \cdot \phi(x)}-\frac{1}{\phi(x)} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{y^2}\left(\frac{d y}{d x}\right)-\frac{1}{y} \cdot \frac{\phi^{\prime}(x)}{\phi(x)}=\frac{-1}{\phi(x)}\end{aligned}$
Let $\mathrm{t}=\frac{-1}{\mathrm{y}} \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{dt}}{\mathrm{dx}}=\frac{1}{\mathrm{y}^2}\left(\frac{\mathrm{dy}}{\mathrm{dx}}\right)\Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{dt}}{\mathrm{dx}}+\mathrm{t} \cdot \frac{\phi^{\prime}(\mathrm{x})}{\phi(\mathrm{x})}=\frac{-1}{\phi(\mathrm{x})}I . F=e^{\int \frac{\phi^{\prime}(x)}{\phi(x)} \cdot d x}=e^{\log \phi(x)}=\phi(x)$
Solution of differential equation is
$\begin{aligned} \mathrm{t} \cdot \phi(\mathrm{x}) & =\int \frac{-1}{\phi(\mathrm{x})} \times \phi(\mathrm{x}) \cdot \mathrm{dx} \\ \Rightarrow \frac{-1}{\mathrm{y}} \phi(\mathrm{x}) & =-\mathrm{x}-\mathrm{c} \Rightarrow \frac{\phi(\mathrm{x})}{\mathrm{y}}=\mathrm{x}+\mathrm{c} \Rightarrow \mathrm{y}=\frac{\phi(\mathrm{x})}{\mathrm{x}+\mathrm{c}}\end{aligned}$

The angles of elevation of the top of a tower from the top and foot of a pole are respectively $30^{\circ}$ and $45^{\circ}$. If $\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{T}}$ is the height of the tower and $h_p$ is the height of the pole, then which of the following are correct?

Select the correct answer using the code given below.

Let the distance between tower and pole be ' $x$ '.
$\begin{aligned} & \tan 45^{\circ}=\frac{\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{t}}}{\mathrm{x}} \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{t}}}{\mathrm{x}}=1 \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{~h}_{\mathrm{t}}=\mathrm{x} .\end{aligned}$ Now, $\tan 30^{\circ}=\frac{h_{\mathrm{t}}-\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{p}}}{\mathrm{x}} \Rightarrow \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}=\frac{\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{t}}-\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{p}}}{\mathrm{x}}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}=\frac{\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{t}}-\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{p}}}{\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{t}}} \\ & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}-1}=\frac{\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{t}}-\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{p}}}{\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{t}}-\left(\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{t}}-\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{p}}\right)}\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \frac{\sqrt{3}+1}{2}=\frac{\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{t}}-\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{p}}}{\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{p}}} \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{t}}-\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{p}}}{\sqrt{3}+1}=\frac{\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{p}}}{2}$\ldots(1) So, statement ' 2 ' is correct. Now, $\frac{h_t-h_p}{h_p}=\frac{\sqrt{3}+1}{2} \Rightarrow \frac{h_t-h_p+2 h_p}{h_p}=\frac{\sqrt{3}+1+4}{2}\Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{t}}+\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{p}}}{\mathrm{h}_{\mathrm{p}}}=\frac{5+\sqrt{3}}{2}$\ldots(2) So, statement ‘3’ is incorrect.

Product of the roots $(\mathrm{P})=\left(\alpha+\beta^{-1}\right)\left(\beta+\alpha^{-1}\right)=\left(\alpha+\frac{1}{\beta}\right)\left(\beta+\frac{1}{\alpha}\right)=\alpha \beta+1+1+\frac{1}{\alpha \beta}=\alpha \beta+2+\frac{1}{\alpha \beta}=\frac{1}{3}+2+\frac{1}{\frac{1}{3}}=\frac{1}{3}+2+3=\frac{1}{3}+5=\frac{16}{3}$.
So, the required equation is $x^2-S . x .+P=0=x^2+\frac{8}{3} x+\frac{16}{3}=0 \Rightarrow 3 x^2+8 x+16=0$

For the first 10 minutes, he has counted $150 \times 10=1500$ notes.
Time taken to count remaining 3000 notes
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{S}_{\mathrm{n}}=\frac{\mathrm{n}}{2}[2 \mathrm{a}+(\mathrm{n}-1) \mathrm{d}] \\ & \Rightarrow 3000=\frac{\mathrm{n}}{2}[2 \times 148+(\mathrm{n}-1)(-2)]\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow 3000=\frac{\mathrm{n}}{2} \times 2(148-\mathrm{n}+1) \\ & \Rightarrow 3000=148 \mathrm{n}-\mathrm{n}^2+\mathrm{n} \\ & \Rightarrow \mathrm{n}^2-149 \mathrm{n}+3000=0\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}& \Rightarrow(\mathrm{n}-24)(\mathrm{n}-125) \\
& \Rightarrow \mathrm{n}=24, \text { or } \mathrm{n}=125 .
\end{aligned}$
Since he has taken 10 minutes to count 1500 notes, he will not take 125 min to count 3000 notes.
So, $\mathrm{n}=24$.
$\therefore$ Total time $=10+24=34$ minutes.
